content:
That shows that the profile Thunderbird is expecting is on drive D. It also appears that this was a custom setup. My suggestion is this:

  1. browse the appdata\thunderbird\profiles folder to confirm the profile you want
  2. then, use the profile manager to create the appropriate profiles.ini to launch that profile. Instructions for that are at https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/profile-manager-create-and-remove-thunderbird-profiles

Another, possibly easier approach, would be this:

  1. copy your appdata\roaming\thunderbird folder elsewhere and then delete the one at appdata\roaming
  2. reinstall thunderbird, which will create a basic profile
  3. exit thunderbird
  4. now, browse the profiles.ini file to see the name of the profile set as default
  5. copy the actual profile you want within the backup you just did (just the profile itself, not the thunderbird folder), and place in the appdata\roaming\thunderbird\profiles folder
  6. finally, delete the basic profile and rename yours to the same name.
  7. restart thunderbird

This is true when you have Icons + Text showing. For a more compact setup, I opt for Icons only. TB correctly offers that option which is essential with smaller screens. As my screenshots show, the View button doesn't change to show that anything other than All is active. As I discover from time to time, this can be a huge problem because TB remembers your selection for each folder and between sessions until you change it again (which is good thing BTW).

So, a few days ago I spent hours (literally) trying to figure out why many messages appeared to be missing from a certain folder. I nearly contacted my ISP but then their webmail showed the missing messages. After many tests I realised that I had applied a View to that specific folder long a time ago, I had forgotten about it, and when I reopened the folder the filter was still active.

The button could show that a filter is applied. It could look depressed. Alternatively, the next button in my screenshot shows a blue light and it works well. A file manager (Free Commander) changed the background of the folder pane to indicate a filtering mode was applied, therefore not all files were showing.

I must say without some visual feedback with Icons only, sooner or later the feature proves enormously counterproductive.

I am pleased that all works. Now, on the Outboxes: You have touched one of my weak areas, and forgiveness may not occur. :) There are true geniuses here, and I am not one. My style is to figure out how to remove the problem, not necessarily the purest way. For example, I recently set up a gmx account on my PC with unified view. But I noticed that in a separate entry was an Outbox. What the heck is that? My guess is that it is for mail ready to send later. So I just unsubscribed it and it disappeared. From my perspective, the problem is solved. So, in your case, I would first check to see if an Outbox folder serves your needs with a trial. Then unsubscribe from the other one. Okay, not pure and not very technical, but life is short and I do not want "Knows how to remove Outbox' on my grave marker. :) See if you can just unscribe it. And then celebrate that your system is working. For a BACKUP, I suggest doing this::

  1. exit thunderbird
  2. copy the appdata\roaming\thunderbird folder to external media
  3. also copy D:\Mail to external media

Should you need to restore, do this:

  1. install and exit thunderbird
  2. at appdata\roaming\ DELETE the thunderbird folder
  3. copy your backup Thunderbird folder to appdata\roaming
  4. place your backed up profile on drive D with same name of Mail
  5. start thunderbird and you're done

Finally print or otherwise save this post so that you have the info for next time. People often forget that their profile is not on the C drive and then are puzzled when a restore doesn't work.

It was fun assisting you. I'm glad all is working. :)
